name: CASH, the Hon. Michaelia Clare

headline.note: Official, employer-adjacent and first-person biographies consistently identify Cash's legal career at Freehills from 1999 until entering the Senate in 2008. They do not publish exact appointment/cessation dates, hours, leave or campaign arrangements. The 1990-99 period contains travel and legal study but no sufficiently documented employment chronology. No full-time private-sector total is calculated.

career_spells.role: Solicitor and senior associate, employment and industrial relations
career_spells.evidence_note: The official parliamentary biography and multiple professional/party biographies record legal practice at Freehills from 1999 to entry into Parliament in 2008, ultimately as a senior associate in employment and industrial relations. The exact 1999 start, promotion date, hours, leave, election campaign arrangements and final day are not published; 1 July 2008 is the Senate term start, not proved as the employment cessation date.
career_spells.counting_note: Private employment is well supported, but substantive full-time status, exact boundaries and leave are insufficient for a documented full-time-years calculation.

career_spells.evidence_note: Biographies record Young Liberal, state-council, divisional and state-executive activity before Senate election. No paid party employment is established.
career_spells.counting_note: Party and candidate activity is excluded.

career_spells.evidence_note: The official parliamentary biography records election in 2007 with the Senate term beginning 1 July 2008 and subsequent re-elections.

research_notes: Identify any paid employment between Cash's 1990 Curtin graduation and 1999 Freehills commencement, distinguishing overseas travel and legal study from employment.
Obtain Freehills appointment, admission and promotion dates, hours, leave and exact cessation, including the 2007 election campaign and interval before the Senate term began on 1 July 2008.
Confirm whether any Liberal Party position was paid employment rather than party governance or candidacy.
